evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md is a first-person request from a recruiting team: line 1 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day? ... Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts.' Lines 3-9 describe needs in user terms ('I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none, and I need to be able to undo my last move', 'If a message arrives while I am reading further up, leave my place alone and just tell me there is something new', 'They must never see our internal notes, why someone was rejected, or anyone else.'). A grep for headings, numbered items, bullets, 'shall' or 'MUST' in instruction.md returns 0 matches: no acceptance list, spec table or feature matrix (quality-checks.md:11 defect forms). Line 11 explicitly leaves design open ('layout and names are yours') and delegates exact rules to /instructions/hireops_rules.md, a separate team notes doc, which is the template's intended split (template environment/instructions/notes.md). The only recipe-like content is line 13 (Node.js/Express/SQLite, node /app/server.js, port 3000/PORT, GET /api/health, /app/app.db/DB_PATH) and line 15 (copy into /app, seed once). These restate the shared runtime contract in template integration.md:3-14 that the harness depends on, not a task-authored build recipe; the line itself says 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call' and is phrased conversationally ('Server dependencies are already available, so don't install packages'). Line 17 credentials are expected by the delivery profile (SKILL.md Known false positives). Counterexample search: a stricter reading could call line 13 a 'build recipe (framework ... endpoint list)'; rejected because it names one platform-mandated health endpoint and the template runtime, not a file layout or route list, and removing it would break the template contract. This row grades prose only; no app behaviour, runtime run or score is implied by this Pass.
